title: Past simple (I did)
subtitle: I did
summary: Use the past simple for completed actions and situations in the past, with did/didn't for questions and negatives and was/were for be.

lesson.heading: Study this example
lesson.text: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart was an Austrian musician and composer. He **lived** from 1756 to 1791. He **started** composing at the age of five and **wrote** more than 600 pieces of music. He **was** only 35 years old when he **died**. lived / started / wrote / was / died are all past simple: finished actions and situations in the past.

examples.text: He **was** only 35 years old when he **died**.

lesson.heading: Regular verbs: -ed
lesson.text: Very often the past simple ends in **-ed** (regular verbs). Watch the spelling: stop - stopped, study - studied.

examples.text: I work in a travel agency now. Before that I **worked** in a department store.
They **invited** us to their party, but we **decided** not to go.
The police **stopped** me on my way home last night.
Laura **passed** her exam because she **studied** very hard.

lesson.heading: Irregular verbs
rows: Mozart **wrote** more than 600 pieces of music.
We **saw** Alice in town a few days ago.
I **went** to the cinema three times last week.
It was cold, so I **shut** the window.
lesson.note: Many verbs are irregular: the past simple does not end in -ed.

lesson.heading: Questions and negatives: did/didn't
lesson.text: In questions and negative sentences we use **did/didn't + infinitive** (enjoy/see/go etc.): *did you enjoy?*, *she didn't see*, *did they go?*. Sometimes **do** is the main verb of the sentence (did you do?, I didn't do).

examples.text: I enjoyed the party a lot. **Did you enjoy** it?
How many people **did they invite** to the wedding?
I **didn't buy** anything because I **didn't have** any money.
What **did you do** at the weekend?
examples.wrong: What did you at the weekend?

lesson.heading: The past of be: was/were
lesson.text: The past of **am/is** is **was** (I/he/she/it was, wasn't) and the past of **are** is **were** (we/you/they were, weren't). Questions simply change the order: *was I?*, *were you?* - no did.

examples.text: **Was** the weather good when you **were** on holiday?
They **weren't** able to come because they **were** so busy.
I **wasn't** hungry, so I **didn't eat** anything.
**Did you go** out last night or **were you** too tired?

lesson.text: After did/didn't the verb goes back to the infinitive: Did you see? I didn't go. But was/were never take did: Was it good? (not Did it be good?)

exercises.prompt: Yesterday was a typical working day for Laura. She ___ a big breakfast.
The film wasn't very good. I ___ it much.
Match each verb with its irregular past simple form.
'How did you learn to drive?' 'My father ___ me.'
Is the past form regular (-ed) or irregular?
James drove from San Francisco to Denver. Ask him how long the trip took.
exercises.explanation: Question: question word + did + subject + infinitive.

exercises.prompt: Ask James where he stayed on his trip - in hotels?
exercises.explanation: Where + did + subject + infinitive (stay, not stayed).

exercises.statement: What did you at the weekend?
exercises.explanation: What did you do at the weekend? do is the main verb, so we need did ... do.

exercises.statement: Was the weather good when you were on holiday?
exercises.explanation: Correct. Questions with be use was/were without did.

exercises.prompt: It was hard carrying the bags. They ___ really heavy.
The bed was very uncomfortable. I ___ well.
I didn't like the hotel. The room ___ very clean.
exercises.explanation: The negative past of is: wasn't (no did with be).
